_meta.indication: JASCAYD is indicated for the treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) in adult patients.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter study; subjects randomized 1:1:1 to 9 mg BID, 18 mg BID, or placebo, stratified by antifibrotic use, for a minimum of 52 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), on or off antifibrotics
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: absolute change from baseline in FVC at Week 52
pivotal_trials.n: N=1177 randomized (392 at 9 mg BID, 392 at 18 mg BID, 393 placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: Both doses statistically significant vs placebo: 18 mg treatment difference 68.8 mL (p=0.0005); 9 mg treatment difference 44.8 mL (p=0.0223)

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study over 12 weeks evaluating nerandomilast 18 mg BID vs placebo
pivotal_trials.population: IPF subjects on or off approved antifibrotics
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: change from baseline in FVC at Week 12
pivotal_trials.n: 147 IPF subjects randomized (97 treated with nerandomilast 18 mg BID, 50 placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: Demonstrated a significant reduction in decline of FVC with nerandomilast vs placebo; adjusted mean difference versus placebo in FVC at Week 12 was 102 mL (non-AF group) and 80.4 mL (AF group)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%): diarrhea (42% at 18 mg, 31% at 9 mg vs 17% placebo), COVID-19, upper respiratory tract infection, depression, weight decreased, decreased appetite, nausea, fatigue, headache, vomiting, back pain, and dizziness. Diarrhea was the most frequent adverse reaction leading to discontinuation (6% at 18 mg, 2% at 9 mg).
target_moa: Oral inhibitor of phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) with at least nine-fold preferential inhibition of the PDE4B isoenzyme; PDE4B inhibition raises intracellular cAMP and reduces pro-fibrotic growth factors and inflammatory cytokines, exerting antifibrotic and immunomodulatory effects

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting or external consultation was required for this application

basis.text: Granted February 10, 2022 based on Study 13, which demonstrated a significant improvement in FVC in subjects on and off antifibrotic therapies

basis.text: NDA reviewed on a priority timeline (Priority review); PDUFA goal date 10/7/2025

citations.quote: Given that benefits observed in Study 13 were further confirmed in Study 14, NDA 218764 for nerandomilast was reviewed on a priority timeline.

summary.text: Nerandomilast received breakthrough therapy designation (Feb 2022) and orphan drug designation for IPF, and the NDA was reviewed on a priority timeline; it was approved via traditional (full) approval based on two adequate and well-controlled studies, not accelerated approval.

citations.quote: Nerandomilast received breakthrough therapy designation on February 10, 2022, based on results from Study 13, which demonstrated a significant improvement in FVC in subjects on and off antifibrotic therapies.
A pediatric assessment was not required for NDA 218764 as nerandomilast received orphan designation for IPF.

The substantial evidence of effectiveness (SEE) of nerandomilast in patients with IPF was established using data from two adequate and well-controlled studies: Study 1305-0013 (Study 13) and Study 1305-0014 (Study 14).
